The walk

How the job actually happens

01

Walk and flag

We tie orange ribbon on every oak, pine or sweetgum you want to keep. Nothing gets cut without your say-so.

02

Mark the pad

Your builder's stakes become a cleared driveway path and house pad, graded so water runs away.

03

Mulch the understory

Yaupon, briars and saplings ground into mulch on the spot. Nothing hauled, nothing burned.

04

Final walk

We walk it again with you before we load the machine. Every ribbon-marked tree still standing.

What we clear

Eight ways to open the land

  • Homesite lot clearing

    A cleared pad and driveway path cut around the trees you flagged to keep.

    Price it

  • Forestry mulching

    Brush and small trees ground into mulch on the spot, nothing to haul or burn.

    Price it

  • Yaupon and underbrush clearing

    The yaupon wall under your pines thinned out so you can see and walk the woods.

    Price it

  • Stump grinding

    Stumps ground below the surface so you can mow, seed or build right over them.

    Price it

  • Fence line clearing

    A clean strip along your fence so the wire can be fixed and kept up.

    Price it

  • Trail and driveway cutting

    A walking trail or truck path cut through the woods, wide enough for what you drive.

    Price it

  • Tree removal

    Dead or leaning pines and sweetgums dropped away from the house and cleaned up.

    Price it

  • Site prep and grading

    Roots raked out and the pad graded so your builder can start on firm ground.

    Price it
